tested_scope.scope_guard: Finite abstract model only. GitHub immutable-release observations are source-qualified mechanism properties, not a claim that every repository has the feature enabled or that arbitrary external sinks inherit these semantics.

observations: When immutable releases are enabled, a published release's tag is locked while the release exists and release assets cannot be modified or deleted.
If the immutable release is deleted, its tag may be deleted, but the same tag name cannot be reused.

GitHub documents protection against repository resurrection attacks: deleting and recreating a repository with the same name does not permit reuse of tag names that were associated with immutable releases in the original repository.
Release immutability is an opt-in repository or organization setting and applies only to future releases.

model_definition.mutable_sink_cas: Identity is lost when target restore and journal/transition retention loss coincide. A rewound repository can then authorize stale state; ambiguous response plus takeover can duplicate the effect after identity loss.
model_definition.append_only_target_journal: Append-only protects only while the journal remains in the target's surviving incarnation. Retention/visibility loss or restore+ABA removes the evidence needed for freshness or retry reconciliation.
model_definition.github_immutable_release_tag_oracle: Already-published transition tag names remain non-reusable even after immutable-release deletion and repository resurrection, so replay of the same stable transition ID stays fenced. But release deletion removes a visible latest-generation witness; an unused stale lower-generation transition name can still be newly introduced after rollback because tag anti-reuse is per-name, not a visible monotonic minimum-generation floor.
model_definition.hypothetical_independent_floor: An external-to-rollback-domain monotonic minimum generation/effect floor rejects every stale or duplicate transition; retained only as a non-accepted comparison control.

new_evidence.positive_narrowing: GitHub immutable release tag-name non-reuse is stronger than mutable target CAS for stable transition-ID replay: in this model it removed all 8 ambiguous-response/takeover duplicate-authoritative-effect cases and remained replay-fencing even across release deletion/repository resurrection.
new_evidence.falsification: That property is not a standalone anti-rollback freshness floor. In 16 repository-rewind + target-restore + latest-witness-visibility-loss scenarios, a previously unused stale lower-generation transition remains admissible in the model because per-name non-reuse does not reveal the deleted latest generation.
new_evidence.minimal_unresolved_child: A repository/target-native read-visible monotonic minimum-generation witness whose latest value cannot be rolled back, deleted, compacted or hidden by target restore/delete-recreate, and whose validation is in the same authority/effect boundary, without richer-mode/protected/manual execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, external hosted coordination, or incremental monetary cost.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.note: Immutable releases were evaluated as a public mechanism property only; this role did not enable or alter repository settings. Even assuming the feature is already enabled, the tested standalone mechanism fails the freshness floor, so no admin/setup dependency is packaged as an accepted route.
